fact_check_verdict: Single-outlet story (Juneau Empire, Jeffrey Kennett, November 14th) plus the state's own notice listing confirming title, agency, date and ID 225838 (body 403, no attachments). Every claim about the draft is spoken as PROPOSED or DRAFT and attributed to the Juneau Empire. No reason for the AI and automated tools clause, no comment deadline and no named official appear anywhere, so the film asserts none. Current-law claims rest on 2 AAC 96 (Cornell LII) and AS 40.25 (FindLaw). Never say the first five hours are free today.

claims.spoken: On November 11th, Alaska's Department of Administration posted a notice of proposed changes to its public records regulations.
claims.on_screen: NOTICE OF PROPOSED CHANGES · NOV 11TH
claims.verbatim_source: "Notice of Proposed Changes On Alaska Public Records Act Regulations"

claims.spoken: Under the draft, people couldn't file records requests through third party services or automated tools, including artificial intelligence, the Juneau Empire reports.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · NO REQUESTS VIA AUTOMATED TOOLS OR AI
claims.verbatim_source: "people would be prohibited from submitting records requests through third-party services or automated tools"
requires: give NO reason for the ban

claims.spoken: Agencies could also require requests to come through their own official online forms or portals.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · OFFICIAL FORMS OR PORTALS ONLY
claims.verbatim_source: "Agencies could also require requests to be filed through their official online forms or portals."

claims.spoken: Today's rules say an agency can't deny a request just because it isn't on the agency's form.
claims.on_screen: CURRENT RULE · NO DENIAL FOR SKIPPING THE FORM
claims.verbatim_source: "a request may not be denied solely because it is not on that form"
requires: don't say the draft repeals it

claims.spoken: Current rules even count a spoken request as a valid one.
claims.on_screen: CURRENT RULE · ORAL REQUESTS COUNT
claims.verbatim_source: "An oral request for records is considered a valid request under this chapter."

claims.spoken: The draft would let agencies stop work after reviewing 250 documents or spending 15 staff hours.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · STOP AT 250 DOCUMENTS OR 15 HOURS
claims.verbatim_source: "reviewing 250 documents or spending 15 staff hours completing production tasks"

claims.spoken: If a request tops five hours of work in a month, agencies would charge for all of it, including the first five hours.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · PAST 5 HOURS, PAY FOR ALL OF IT
claims.verbatim_source: "once exceeded, agencies would charge for all applicable search and copying time, including the first five hours"
requires: do NOT claim the first five hours are free today

claims.spoken: State law already sets a fee trigger once one requester's records take more than five person hours in a month.
claims.on_screen: STATE LAW · FEES START PAST 5 HOURS A MONTH
claims.verbatim_source: "If the production of records for one requester in a calendar month exceeds five person-hours,"
requires: don't describe the current hours as free

claims.spoken: Fees could still be reduced or waived when releasing records serves the public interest.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · PUBLIC INTEREST WAIVER STAYS
claims.verbatim_source: "charges could still be reduced or waived if releasing the records serves the public interest"

claims.spoken: The window to appeal a denial would shrink from 60 working days to 30.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · APPEAL WINDOW 60 TO 30 WORKING DAYS
claims.verbatim_source: "Current rules allow 60 working days to contest a denial, but the proposal would cut that deadline to 30 working days."

claims.spoken: Current rules give 60 working days to appeal after a denial is issued.
claims.on_screen: CURRENT RULE · 60 WORKING DAYS TO APPEAL
claims.verbatim_source: "within 60 working days after the denial is issued"

claims.spoken: Agencies would keep the same 10 working days to respond.
claims.on_screen: 10 WORKING DAYS TO RESPOND · UNCHANGED
claims.verbatim_source: "not later than the 10th working day after the date the agency receives a request"
requires: extensions exist, not a hard ceiling

claims.spoken: Agencies could reject requests made for financial or commercial gain.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · REJECT REQUESTS FOR COMMERCIAL GAIN
claims.verbatim_source: "reject requests made for financial or commercial gain"

claims.spoken: They could also turn away requests seeking personal information about another person.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · REJECT REQUESTS FOR SOMEONE ELSE'S PERSONAL INFO
claims.verbatim_source: "to obtain personal information about another person"

claims.spoken: Alaska residents could get priority over nonresidents.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · RESIDENTS GET PRIORITY
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska residents could receive priority over nonresidents when seeking public records under the proposed rules"
requires: say PRIORITY, not a ban on nonresidents

claims.spoken: State law says every person has a right to inspect a public record in the state.
claims.on_screen: "EVERY PERSON HAS A RIGHT TO INSPECT"
claims.verbatim_source: "Every person has a right to inspect a public record in the state, including public records in recorders' offices, except"
requires: the statute has exceptions, don't say every record
don't call the residency priority illegal

claims.spoken: Agencies could also refuse to reproduce entire databases.
claims.on_screen: PROPOSED · NO COPIES OF WHOLE DATABASES
claims.verbatim_source: "Agencies could also refuse to reproduce entire databases"

claims.spoken: The rules would cover executive branch agencies, not the Legislature, the courts or the University of Alaska.
claims.on_screen: NOT COVERED · LEGISLATURE · COURTS · UNIVERSITY
claims.verbatim_source: "The Alaska Legislature, state courts and University of Alaska system would also fall outside the proposal"

claims.spoken: The department's filing says the changes are meant to improve efficiency and would cost nothing extra to put in place.
claims.on_screen: STATED AIM · EFFICIENCY · NO ADDED COST
claims.verbatim_source: "the revisions were intended to improve efficiency, and that the department estimated no additional cost to implement the regulations"
requires: attribute to the department's filing AS REPORTED BY JUNEAU EMPIRE
a general aim, NOT a reason for the AI clause, keep them apart

claims.spoken: A records bill, House Bill 377, stalled in the House State Affairs Committee this year.
claims.on_screen: HB 377 · STALLED IN HOUSE STATE AFFAIRS
claims.verbatim_source: "The legislation stalled in the House State Affairs Committee"
requires: don't say the rule copies HB 377

cut: any reason for the AI clause
second outlet for the AI clause
